spuelbar.text: “Flushable” only means: it slides through the toilet. It does not mean: it dissolves. Toilet paper falls apart in water within seconds. Wet wipes are made to be tear-proof – even the “flushable” ones often stay in one piece in the sewer for hours. There is no legal test standard for the word “flushable” – every manufacturer can print it on the pack. So: always put them in the general waste.

info.intro: Come along on the journey! This is how the water from your toilet gets back into the river clean.
info.station.haus.text: Everything from the toilet, shower, washing machine and sink flows into the house connection pipe. It is often only as thick as a forearm – one nappy is enough to block it.
info.station.kanal.text: The wastewater sewer lies under the street. The wastewater flows all by itself down a gentle slope. Fat cools down here and sticks to the pipe walls.
info.station.pumpe.text: Where the ground stops sloping, pumps lift the wastewater. Here wet wipes, dental floss and hair wind themselves into thick ropes around the impellers – and the pump stops.
info.station.rechen.text: A large screen fishes out all the coarse stuff that should never have gone down the toilet. Then sand and small stones settle, and fat is skimmed off.
info.station.becken.text: Now billions of tiny bacteria get to work: they eat the dirt out of the water. Chemicals and medicines can make them sick – or are not broken down at all.
info.station.fluss.text: The cleaned water flows into the river. Whatever the treatment plant could not remove – microplastics or drug residues – swims along to fish and plants.
info.gully.titel: And the drain in the street?
info.gully.text: Here we have two separate sewers: one for wastewater and one for rainwater. Whatever goes into the street drain flows directly into the stream without any treatment. So: no mop water, no car-wash water, no cigarette butts and no leaves in the drain!
info.grafik.beschreibung: Separate sewer system: wastewater from the house flows to the treatment plant and is cleaned. Rainwater from the street drain flows untreated directly into the stream.
